glossary.gallbladder: Small sac under the liver that stores and concentrates bile.
glossary.LFTs: Liver function tests: blood tests of bilirubin and liver enzymes.
glossary.inflammatory markers: Blood tests such as CRP and WCC that rise with inflammation or infection.
glossary.Crohn's disease: Inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gut, often the terminal ileum.
glossary.ileal resection: Surgical removal of part of the ileum, the last part of the small intestine.
glossary.bile salt: Detergent-like molecule in bile that keeps cholesterol dissolved and helps absorb fat.
glossary.reabsorption: Taking a substance back into the blood, here bile salts from the ileum.
glossary.RUQ: Right upper quadrant of the abdomen.
glossary.colicky: Pain that comes in waves as a hollow organ squeezes against a blockage.
glossary.swinging fevers: Temperature that rises and falls sharply, typical of a collection of pus.
glossary.small bowel obstruction: Blockage of the small intestine causing vomiting, distension and colicky pain.
glossary.jaundice: Yellow skin and eyes from raised bilirubin.
glossary.abdominal ultrasound: Imaging of the abdomen with sound waves; first choice for gallstones.
glossary.hepatobiliary: Relating to the liver, gallbladder and bile ducts.
glossary.opioid: Strong painkiller acting on opioid receptors, such as morphine.
glossary.contraindicated: Should not be used because it could cause harm in this patient.
glossary.incidental: Found by chance while looking for something else.
glossary.elective: Planned in advance rather than done as an emergency.
glossary.percutaneous: Done through the skin, usually with a needle or tube under image guidance.
glossary.milking: Squeezing a stuck gallstone along the bowel by hand during surgery.
glossary.bilious: Containing bile, so green or yellow.
glossary.phospholipids: Fat molecules in bile that, with bile salts, keep cholesterol dissolved.
glossary.spasm: Sudden involuntary contraction of a muscle wall.
glossary.superinfection: A new infection on top of an existing problem.
glossary.bile salt pool: The total amount of bile salts the body recycles between the liver and gut.
glossary.cholesterol saturation: How close bile is to holding the maximum cholesterol it can keep dissolved.
glossary.proximally: Towards the start, here back up the bowel.
